competences: access to complementary agricultural research collaborations.

knowledge_transfer.statement: The transfer is genuinely bidirectional: crop physiology/agronomy <-> geospatial/data science.

partner_contributions.heading: MATE -> FIELDWISE
partner_contributions.statement: MATE provides the long-term experimental knowledge and source-domain dataset necessary for model development and validation. Its contribution is central to historical data, processing-tomato experiments, hyperspectral measurements, soil/weather observations and prospective validation.

partner_contributions.heading: MVCRI -> FIELDWISE
partner_contributions.statement: MVCRI provides the independent Bulgarian research environment required for cross-country scientific transferability. Its role is specifically Hungary -> Bulgaria rather than simply increasing sample size.

partner_contributions.heading: AgroVIR -> FIELDWISE
partner_contributions.statement: AgroVIR provides the bridge from research field to farmer field and from research prototype to operational requirements. This produces a genuine academic-research-industry knowledge chain.

capacity_statements.heading: ELTE - MSCA beneficiary
capacity_statements.statement: Primary methodological and training environment: geoinformatics, EO, advanced modelling, uncertainty, transferability and research integration.

capacity_statements.statement: Provides five-year data, processing-tomato experimental environment, hyperspectral/soil/weather information and primary scientific validation.

capacity_statements.heading: MVCRI, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy - geographic transfer environment
capacity_statements.statement: Provides an independent processing-tomato environment, contrasting country/agro-climate and cross-country model validation and calibration.

capacity_statements.heading: AgroVIR - operational transfer environment
capacity_statements.statement: Provides commercial farmer-field testing, research-to-operation transferability, MVP requirements/interoperability evaluation and a prospective FMIS integration pathway.

training_and_career.statement: The fellowship will provide advanced competence in Bayesian/probabilistic modelling, uncertainty quantification, spatio-temporal validation, sensor-domain transfer, cross-country adaptation, operational AI evaluation, research-to-MVP translation and IP/exploitation.
FIELDWISE will address the remaining competence gap in Bayesian modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor transfer, uncertainty, domain adaptation and decision evaluation.
Intended career progression: Plant Physiologist/Agronomist -> EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist -> Independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence.

participant_capacity.recent_projects_and_publications_note: Answered on 2026-08-14 on its publications half, closing the deferral of 2026-08-11. The deferral stood because CORDIS indexes participants at university level, so an ELTE query returns faculty-wide projects with no connection to the Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics, and only Prof. Jung or the institute could supply the group's own record. The operator supplied it from Prof. Jung's ORCID record. Recorded Confirmed rather than Assumed because each of the four items was checked against the publisher's own record for its DOI on 2026-08-14 — MDPI for the three journal articles, OpenAlex for the IEEE letter — with title, journal, date and author list matching in every case, and because Prof. Jung is an author on all four, so this is the supervisor's own output rather than the faculty-wide query the deferral rejected. Two things §3.2 must respect. The field's projects half is still not supplied: no institute project list was given, none is inferred here, and §3.2 therefore states recent publications and says nothing about the institute's project portfolio. And the four are not of equal use. The three 2025 items are Earth-observation and agricultural-monitoring work and carry the §3.2 argument; the 2024 IEEE letter is building-structure vectorisation and belongs at most as evidence of deep-learning method breadth, not as EO-for-agriculture capacity. Two of the three also sit in a DLI and light-mapping line with Sipos and Varga, which is adjacent to, and not the same as, the crop-stress remote sensing FIELDWISE needs; §3.2 should claim the adjacency rather than overstate it.

participant_capacity.organisation_profile: AgroVIR Kft., founded 2007 and seated in Budaörs, Hungary, develops and operates a cloud-based farm management information system built on twenty years of practice in Hungarian commercial agriculture. The platform is in production use across more than 745,000 hectares in eight countries: Hungary (500,000+ ha), Romania (120,000+), Azerbaijan (50,000+), Slovakia (40,000+), Bulgaria (15,000+), Serbia (10,000+), Ukraine (7,000+) and Argentina (3,000+). This is the commercial-scale operating environment against which WP5 tests research-to-farm transferability, and the Bulgarian and Hungarian footprints match the two countries FIELDWISE works in. The company is registered under NACE 7020 (business and management consulting), reflecting its founding activity; its current business is agricultural software.
participant_capacity.organisation_profile_note: Drafted in input pack item 12 from the company's own published figures and adopted with the item 1 C9 closing clause, which names the registration discrepancy rather than leaving an evaluator to find it.
participant_capacity.infrastructure_and_farm_access: Network access to the AgroVIR platform and its commercial farm base, and validation of the prediction pipeline through the AgroVIR software.

The placeholder does not guess a name either: it identifies the team by the function the placement's own already-answered content requires, which is the only inference the record supports. Two of the three access claims are FMIS development or staging and the customer-data environment, and three of the four six_month_work_content items are operational hardening of the prediction pipeline in a production FMIS environment, the FMIS integration roadmap, and requirements engineering with commercial growers. A fellow with that access doing that work sits with whoever builds and runs the FMIS. So the placeholder is consistent with everything else on the record, and it is still a placeholder: AgroVIR may call the team something else, may split it, or may seat her with an agronomy or customer-facing group instead. Replace it with the team's actual name and composition before submission. It is the field an evaluator uses to test whether the placement is real, so a generic answer here is the weakest point in the placement argument and should be the first of the placeholders to be corrected.

six_month_work_content.supplied_answer_reframed: The operator's first answer was 'developing further the MVP prototype'. The operator then reframed it rather than replacing it, on three grounds. An MSCA placement must serve the fellow's training, not the host company's engineering. The draft itself calls the MVP 'the research-to-operation demonstrator, not the primary scientific objective' (§1.2 ¶158). And §2.2 records the DrR components as the fellow's background IP, so six months spent developing her own prototype inside a commercial partner raises an ownership question the proposal has not addressed.
six_month_work_content.note: The four items map onto WP5 tasks and deliverables the draft already carries: T5.4 and T5.6 to the operational assessment and D5.4, T5.7 to the roadmap and D5.5. The placement therefore deepens existing WP5 content rather than adding a new strand. The background-IP question stays open and is a §2.2 drafting matter, not a Tier 3 fact.
